planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container plants in spring after frost danger passes in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; 'Rubrum' grows rapidly in warm weather into a large multi-stemmed shrub-tree. It dies back to the ground after hard freezes in zone 7-8 but regrows vigorously from the roots.

directions: Plant rooted cuttings or container-grown plants in spring after frost danger passes, in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, where it quickly grows into a large multi-stemmed shrub. 'Rubrum' (Red Confederate Rose) is a solid-color selection of the classic Southern heirloom Confederate rose, opening its single, 4-6 inch flowers already at full deep rose-red to scarlet color and holding that one saturated hue through the day, rather than performing the dramatic white-to-pink-to-red shift of the straight species. Blooming from late summer into fall with large, yellow-centered flowers held at the stem tips, it is a favorite Deep South pass-along plant that roots effortlessly from cuttings set in a glass of water on the windowsill, the same way it has moved from garden to garden for generations. Like the species, it dies back to the ground after hard freezes in zone 7-8 but resprouts vigorously from the root crown each spring and blooms on new wood; prune the previous year's growth back to 2-3 feet in late winter to keep the large shrub-tree in scale.

planting.note: Sow directly where plants are to grow in late spring or early summer for bloom the following year, since this is a biennial or short-lived perennial that flowers on its second-year stalk.

directions: Sow seed directly where plants are to grow in late spring or early summer for bloom the following year, since Creme de Cassis is a biennial or short-lived perennial that flowers on its second-year stalk. Choose a sheltered, full-sun spot with rich, well-drained soil and stake the tall flower spikes against wind. Creme de Cassis produces large, semi-double to fully double flowers in a striking deep wine-red to burgundy shade edged in pale pink with intricate darker veining radiating through each petal, and single and double blooms sometimes appear together on the same stem — a distinctive bicolor picotee effect not found in solid-color hollyhock strains. Plants reach 6-8 feet and bloom over a long midsummer season, drawing bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds. Strip and discard lower leaves showing hollyhock rust promptly, and let a few seed pods mature and drop to keep a self-sustaining stand going.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society — Alcea rosea 'Creme de Cassis'
John Scheepers Kitchen Garden Seeds — Creme de Cassis Hollyhock

planting.note: Sow directly in spring, or start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost for earlier bloom, in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Sow seed directly in spring, or start indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost for earlier bloom, in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. The Halo series was bred by Thompson & Morgan over sixteen years of selection for large, single, bicolor flowers held on tall, sturdy, rugose-leaved spikes. Each bloom carries a bold, contrasting halo ring in its center — 'Halo Candy' opens sugar-pink with a deep purple halo, 'Halo Cerise' opens cerise-pink with a deep purple halo, and 'Halo Blush' opens white with a fuchsia-red halo around a yellow center — giving the plants a distinctive two-tone target-eye look not found in solid-color or picotee-edged hollyhock strains. Plants form a bushy clump of rugose green foliage and send up flower spikes to about 5 feet from early to late summer. As a hardy perennial, stake in windy sites, water at the base to reduce rust, and deadhead spent spikes to prolong bloom.
sources: Thompson & Morgan — Alcea rosea Halo Series breeding notes
Perennial Resource — Alcea rosea Halo Series variety descriptions

common_name: Mont Blanc Annual Mallow (Pure White Rose Mallow)
directions: Direct sow after the last frost once soil has warmed, since this fast-growing annual mallow resents root disturbance and rarely transplants well from cell packs. A Fleuroselect award winner, Mont Blanc produces an abundance of large, satiny, pure white, hibiscus-like flowers with no pink blush or throat marking, held above a naturally bushy, well-branched mound of soft green foliage — the cleanest white-flowered selection in the trimestris group, distinct from the pink-flushed 'Silver Cup' and the deeper cerise-pink 'Ruby Regis'. Thin seedlings to their final spacing early to prevent stretching, pinch young plants once to encourage bushier growth, and deadhead spent blooms to keep the summer-to-frost flowering display going strong. Makes an excellent bright, informal hedge or massed border planting where a pure white backdrop is wanted.
sources: Fleuroselect — Lavatera trimestris 'Mont Blanc' award description
Select Seeds — Lavatera Mont Blanc variety notes
